(WebFetch extraction 22 Nov 2026 ~08:00 GMT — curl returned 403; AFP / Times of Israel, published 22 Nov 2026 04:02 GMT)

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said China and Russia oppose any change to Iran's nuclear doctrine, in an interview published Saturday with the state-run Iran Daily, amid domestic calls for a shift. He said Iran's "official positions remain the same as before."
Iran continues to cite a fatwa from the late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei prohibiting weapons of mass destruction, including nuclear weapons. Hardliners have revived debate over changing the doctrine since wars with Israel and the US damaged Iranian nuclear facilities.
Iran has enriched uranium to levels with no peaceful use and barred international inspectors from its nuclear sites. Mojtaba Khamenei has not issued a decree overturning his father's ruling. Last week, the UN nuclear watchdog urged Iran to take "incremental steps" to allow inspectors back.
